evidence.note: Structured the build by task type — wrote evaluate.py as one handler per protocol (STS, retrieval, classification, clustering, pair_classification, summarization, main). Decomposition by type is real, but the 'Plan:' notes are tactical ('Append STS function') with no upfront ordered milestone plan or per-type done-criteria stated in advance.

Ran an individual smoke test of one dataset per type in sequence (sts_01, classification_01, retrieval_01, summarization_01, pair_classification_01, clustering_03), each with a leaderboard-comparison done-check (e.g. '0.816 matches BIOSSES', 'Arguana ndcg@10=0.502 expected ~0.50'). This is a genuine per-type validate-before-moving-on gate tied to leaderboard agreement — an 8-like feature.

After the per-type spot checks, treated the remaining 37 datasets as a single bulk full run rather than tracked sub-goals; only 6 datasets were ever individually milestoned, the rest only got structural validation. No coverage tracking of individual datasets.

Final phase is structural check + investigating two suspicious scores. No separate milestone was ever established for the CLI contract or the skip-on-failure harness behavior — those were implemented but never gated as their own done-checks.

reasoning: The agent clearly split the work by task type and validated each type against leaderboard expectations before proceeding (steps 28-35), which exceeds the level-5 anchor's 'plan to validate each type' by actually attaching a leaderboard-agreement done-check per type. However, the milestone structure was implicit rather than an explicit ordered plan, the ordering was not sequenced by risk/shared machinery, the 37 datasets were not tracked as coverage sub-goals (only 6 got individual checks), and there were no separate milestones for the CLI contract or skip-and-continue behavior. That places it above 5 but well short of the full level-8 structure.
